title: Enterprise Onboarding, Support Process, Escalation, Integration & QBR Playbook
author: Maya Patel
body:
Purpose
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's standard operating procedures for enterprise customer onboarding, integration, escalation, known issues, support process, and QBR/health check materials. It is intended for Customer Success (CS), Support, Solutions Engineering, and Engineering owners who participate in onboarding and post-sales operations.

Scope
Applies to all enterprise customers (Dedicated and Private plans) and to hosted customers with enterprise support agreements. For self-serve or purely evaluation customers, follow the abbreviated quickstart docs in eng-developer-experience.

Owner & Stakeholders\- Playbook owner: Customer Success (team lead: Maya Patel)\- Support escalation owners: Support (Level 1/2) and Eng-SRE (Level 3)\- Integration engineering: Solutions Engineering and Eng-Private-Deployments\- Security & compliance: Security team for restricted deployments

High-level Onboarding Phases (overview)
1) Pre-sales to Post-sale Handoff (T minus 10 days)
   - Sales creates handoff packet in Gainsight/CRM with contract, SLAs, allowed models, data residency requirements, and account contacts.
   - CS assigns an Onboarding Manager; schedule kickoff within 5 business days of contract signature.
2) Kickoff (Day 0)
   - Attendees: CS Onboarding Manager, Customer Technical Lead, Solutions Engineer, Security/Compliance rep (if required).
   - Agenda: objectives, success criteria, timeline, stakeholders, security & compliance checklist, sample traffic expectations.
3) Integration & Validation (Day 1-14)
   - Tasks: API key generation + scoped permissions, network connectivity tests (VPC peering/Private), sample requests, embedding ingestion flow, auth flow test.
   - Deliverables: integration checklist signed off, sample inference traffic observed, baseline perf metrics (latency p50/p95, errors).
4) Pre-Go-Live (Day 14-21)
   - Load test to validation throughput (see capacity test steps), failure mode tests (network loss, throttling), and SLO confirmation.
   - Documentation handoff: runbooks, runbook playbacks, and alerting thresholds.
5) Go-Live & Watch (Day 21-35)
   - Active monitoring window with daily health checks and CS/SRE check-ins. Transition to regular support & QBR cadence after 30 days.

Integration Checklist (detailed)
- Account & Auth
  - Generate API keys with minimum required scopes. Record key owner and rotation schedule.
  - Confirm role-based access (RBAC) for customer users if using Private plane console.
- Networking
  - If Private/VPC: confirm IP allowlists, route tables, NAT config, firewall rules, and DNS resolution.
  - If on-prem: validate package install, container runtime versions (Docker/ECS/K8s), and local GPU drivers (CUDA/CuDNN versions).
- Data & Security
  - Confirm data residency and retention policy; ensure KMS/HSM integration if required.
  - Verify audit logging configuration and SIEM ingestion.
- Traffic & Limits
  - Establish rate limits, burst policies, and expected token volumes. Configure per-route throttles or rate limit policies in console.
- Observability
  - Add application telemetry: request id propagation, tracing headers, and error tagging. Configure dashboard access for customer.

Sample API Check (curl)
1) Generate scoped API key in Console. 2) Test basic generation: 
curl -X POST https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <CUSTOMER_API_KEY>" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-base-1\",\"input\":\"Hello world\",\"max_tokens\":16}'

Expected result: 200 OK, Start token stream within 300ms for hosted customers (region dependent).

Capacity and Load Validation
- Recommended test: ramp to sustained throughput equal to 2x expected steady-state for 15 minutes. Monitor GPU utilization, queue depth, p95 latency, and error rate.
- Target thresholds for Dedicated customers: GPU utilization <= 85% at steady-state; p95 latency within SLA +/- 20%; error rate < 0.5% during test.

Escalation Playbook
Severity definitions\- Sev 1 (Critical): Production outage impacting all users, high financial or regulatory impact. Initial response goal: 15 minutes.\- Sev 2 (High): Significant feature degradation for many users; workaround exists. Initial response goal: 1 hour.\- Sev 3 (Medium): Partial loss, limited users, or degraded performance. Initial response goal: 4 hours.\- Sev 4 (Low): Informational or minor request; response within 2 business days.

Triage & Routing Flow
1) L1 Support (CS/Support): Confirm incident, collect logs, reproduce, and apply known workaround if available. If not resolvable within severity SLA, escalate to L2.\2) L2 Support (Product/SE): Deep investigation, collaborate with customer to collect artifacts, open engineering ticket with reproducible case and timeline.\3) L3 (Eng-SRE / Eng-Serving-Runtime): Code-level or infra-level fixes, hotpatches, capacity actions, and post-incident remediation.

Escalation Matrix (contacts & responsibilities)
- L1 Support: Support Slack channel #support-enterprise, email support@redwoodinference.com (monitored 24x7 for enterprise SLAs).\- L2: Solutions Engineering on-call rotation (SE-ONCALL), slack @se-rotations.\- L3: Eng-SRE on-call (pager duty escalation), Eng-Serving-Runtime primary owner.

Communication Templates
- Initial customer update (within 30 minutes for Sev1): "We are investigating a production issue affecting X. Our initial diagnosis: [short summary]. Next update in 30 minutes or earlier. Owner: [name, role]."
- Status update cadence: Every 30 minutes for Sev1 until mitigation; hourly for Sev2.
- Postmortem template: Impact summary, timeline, root cause, remediation, action items, owner for each action, and verification plan. Publish to confluence under incident-postmortems and link to status page.

Support Process & Ticket Lifecycle
1) Creation: Tickets created via Zendesk/Jira Service Desk; include severity, customer impact, sample request id, timestamps, and owner.\2) Initial Response: L1 acknowledges within severity SLA and begins triage checklist.\3) Investigation & Escalation: If escalated, attach reproducible case, logs, perf traces, and if necessary, capture a heap/profile snapshot following privacy guidance.\4) Resolution & Verification: L2/L3 deploy fix or mitigation; verify with customer test plan.\5) Closure & Follow-up: Create post-incident actions and schedule verification. Notify customer and close ticket when customer confirms.

Known Issues & Workarounds (Top recurring items)
1) Symptom: Tokenization mismatch for non-UTF8 inputs\   Workaround: Ensure client encodes text as UTF-8; use pre-tokenization validation and normalize Unicode (NFC).\2) Symptom: Increased p95 latency during prefix-heavy prompts\   Workaround: Enable prefix caching for stable prompt fragments and recommend shorter initial system messages or pre-warm KV cache.\3) Symptom: Rate-limited 429s under bursty traffic\   Workaround: Use client-side exponential backoff with jitter and request quota increases for sustained bursts via console request.\4) Symptom: Failed Private deployment due to driver mismatch\   Workaround: Confirm CUDA and CuDNN versions from onprem-packaging reference; apply driver patch or use the provided container images.

Known issues should be linked to the central \"known-issues-and-workarounds\" page and labeled by affected component (runtime, api, network, private-deploy).

Health Checks & QBR Materials
Quarterly Health Check metrics (suggested)\- Reliability: Uptime (SLA %), incidents by severity, MTTD (mean time to detect), MTTR (mean time to remediate).\- Performance: average and p95 latency for generate and embeddings, percent of requests meeting latency SLO.\- Cost & Efficiency: Cost per 1k tokens, utilization of Dedicated pool, cache hit ratio, batching efficiency.\- Adoption & Product: Active integrations, seats using advanced features (function-calling, streaming), number of routes/models in use.\- Quality: Regression alerts fired, eval score trends on critical prompt sets.

QBR Agenda (60-minute template)
1) Executive summary & health scorecard (10 min)\2) Incident recap & reliability plan (10 min)\3) Usage trends & cost review (10 min)\4) Product highlights & roadmap items relevant to customer (10 min)\5) Action items & next steps (10 min)\6) Q&A and open issues (10 min)

Suggested QBR slide deck outline (confluence attachments)
- Slide 1: Cover + customer and CS owners\- Slide 2: Executive health dashboard (uptime, incidents, p95)\- Slide 3: Usage and cost trends (tokens, model mix, cost allocation)\- Slide 4: Key incidents and remediation status\- Slide 5: Roadmap & requested feature timeline\- Slide 6: Action items & owners

Operational Playbooks & Runbooks (appendix)
- Runbook: High latency (p95 > SLA)\  1) Verify if problem is region-wide or isolated to customer.\  2) Check model variants and routing policy; temporarily reroute to lower-latency variant if available.\  3) Check GPU queue depth and autoscaler actions.\  4) Apply mitigations (increase capacity or throttle noisy routes).\  5) Post-action: monitor for 60 minutes, then move to RCA.\- Runbook: Token leakage / unexpected cost spike\  1) Pause suspect API keys and rotate.\  2) Review request logs for high-token routes.\  3) Apply rate limits and contact customer for investigation.

Templates (quick copy-paste)
- Incident initial update:
  Subject: [Sev1] Production outage affecting <feature>
  Body: We are investigating a production issue impacting <customers>. Impact: <short summary>. Initial mitigation: <what we are doing>. Next update: <time>. Owner: <name> (<role>).

- Postmortem summary fields:
  - Title, Date, Impact, Detect time, Mitigate time, Root cause, Actions, Verification plan, Owners.

Ownership & Escalation Contacts (primary)

Maintenance & Versioning
This playbook is versioned quarterly. Major process changes must be approved by CS leadership and Eng-SRE. To propose changes, create a PR against this confluence page draft and request reviewers listed above.
